1.w: And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you⁺ as to spiritual but as to fleshly—as to infants in Christ.

2.w: I gave you⁺ milk to drink, not food, for you⁺ were not yet able. But now you⁺ are still not able,

3.w: for you⁺ are still fleshly. For where jealousy and strife [are] among you⁺, are you⁺ not fleshly and walking according to man?

4.w: For when one may say, “I am indeed of Paul,” and another, “I of Apollos,” are you⁺ not men?

5.w: Who then is Apollos? And who is Paul? Servants through whom you⁺ believed, even as the Lord gave to each.

6.w: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was giving growth.

7.w: So neither the one planting nor the one watering is anything, but [only] God, the One giving growth.

8.w: Now the one planting and the one watering are one, and each will receive [his] own reward according to [his] own labor.

9.w: For we are God’s fellow workers; you⁺ are God’s field, God’s building.

10.w: According to the grace of God having been given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, but another is building upon [it]. But let each one take heed how he builds upon [it].

11.w: For no one is able to lay another foundation besides the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

12.w: Now if anyone builds upon the foundation [with] gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, [or] straw,

13.w: the work of each will become manifest, for the day will make [it] evident, because it is revealed in fire, and the fire itself will prove the work of each, what sort it is.

14.w: If the work of anyone that he built up will remain, he will receive a reward.

15.w: If the work of anyone will be burned up, he will suffer loss; but he himself will be saved, but only as through fire.

16.w: Do you⁺ not know that you⁺ are God’s temple, and the Spirit of God dwells in you⁺?

17.w: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you⁺ are.

18.w: Let no one deceive himself: If anyone thinks [himself] to be wise among you⁺ in this age, let him become foolish, so that he may become wise.

19.w: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it has been written: “[He is] the One catching the wise in their craftiness,”

20.w: and again, “The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile.”

21.w: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours⁺,

22.w: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or [things] present or [things] about to be—all [are] yours⁺,

23.w: and you⁺ [are] of Christ, and Christ [is] of God.
